titulo: Rock salt stops working when it gets too cold.
receta: regla con numero + pregunta de dos bandas; pilar clima_accion, invierno
destinatario: se lo manda alguien que ya palo su vereda a su vecino que tira media bolsa de sal en la entrada y sigue helada
regla_guardable: Rock salt works down to about 15 F (pavement temperature). Below that it barely melts ice.

interaccion.guardar: Rock salt: effective down to about 15°F on the pavement; below that it works very slowly; below about -6°F it stops.
interaccion.comentar: Do you salt before the snow or after? Before or after?

fuentes: University of Minnesota LTAP, SmartWinterSalt, Homeowners: Deicing use (mnltap.umn.edu/guides/smartwintersalt/homeowners/pavement/deicing-use): 'Rock salt, for example, is effective down to about 15°F. Below 15°F, it will work very slowly and will not melt much ice.' Deicers have a minimum practical melting temperature based on pavement temperature, not air temperature. Use deicers selectively and sparingly. Rock salt stops working below about -6°F (Cargill: eutectic about -6°F).

frases.texto: You throw rock salt on your icy steps, and the ice just sits there.
frases.estilo: Dry and punchy, with a half smile.

frases.texto: That's because salt has a limit.
Rock salt works down to about fifteen degrees Fahrenheit. Below that, it works very slowly and barely melts any ice.
And that's the pavement temperature, not the air temperature.
Below about minus six, it stops working altogether.
Heads up: use deicer selectively and sparingly.
Save this: rock salt works down to about fifteen degrees on the pavement.
Do you salt before the snow or after? Before or after?
Send this to the neighbor who dumps a whole bag on the driveway.
